# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section B concluded + beginning of C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**5:1** And-concerning [...] the daughters of-Israel and-the-holy-seed [...] and-that one-should-not [...] a woman who-is a prostitute [...]

**5:2** [...] for [...] the holy-seed of-the-sons-of-Aaron [...] and-also the seed of-Israel [...]

**5:3** [...] and-one-should-not let the holy-seed become-mixed with [...] and-one-should-not allow [...]

**5:4** [...] for they are holy [...] and-it is written: "you-shall-not bring the hire of-a-prostitute into the house of-the-LORD your God" [...]

**5:5** And-concerning the tithe of-the-grain, the wine, and-the-oil: the priests should-be [...] the first to-extend their hands to-the-first-fruits [...]

**5:6** [...] and-the-Levites [...] shall-receive the tithe [...] from the sons-of-Israel [...]

**5:7** [...] and-concerning the tithe of-the-tithe [...] the priests shall-receive from-the-Levites [...]

**5:8** [...] for [...] we consider that the tithe of-the-grain is like the first-fruits [...] to-the-priests [...]

**5:9** [...] and-one-should-not delay the tithe [...] for these are holy-things [...]

**5:10** And-concerning [...] the Ammonite and-the-Moabite and-the-bastard and-the-eunuch should-not enter the assembly [...]

**5:11** [...] and-they-should-not [...] take-wives from-them [...] nor-should-they-be-admitted [...]

**5:12** [...] for [...] the assembly of-the-LORD is holy [...] and-it is written [...]

**5:13** [...] and-concerning the leper [...] the one-who-has the plague of-leprosy [...] should-not come to-the-holy-purity [...]

**5:14** [...] until the sun sets on the eighth day [...] and-he-has-been purified [...]

**5:15** You know that we have-separated-ourselves from the majority of-the-peo[ple and-from-all] their uncleanness

**5:16** and-from being-joined with-these-matters and-from participating [...] in-these-things [...]

**5:17** [...] and-you know that there-is-not found in-us [...] unfaithfulness to-any of-these-matters [...]

**5:18** [...] for [...] we have-separated for-the-sake-of these-things [...]

**5:19** [...] and-we have [...] withdrawn from the midst of-the-multitude [...] and-from-all their impure deeds [...]

**5:20** And-concerning [...] we-have-written to-you that-you-should-understand the book of-Moses [and the words of-the-prophets and-of-David...]

**5:21** [...] and-the-annals of-each generation [...] and-in the book it-is-written [...]

**5:22** [...] that [...] you would-turn-away from the path [...] and-that-evil would-come-upon-you [...]

**5:23** [...] and-it is written: "and-it-shall-come-to-pass when all these-things come-upon-you" [...]

**5:24** [...] "in-the-end of-days, the blessing and-the-curse" [...]

**5:25** [...] "and-you-shall-take-it to-your-heart and-you-shall-return to-Him with-all your heart and-with-all your soul" [...]

---

*EMET notes: The final halakhic rulings in Section B address marriage purity (5:1–4, citing Deut 23:18), tithing order (5:5–9), assembly exclusions (5:10–12, citing Deut 23:2–4), and leprosy regulations (5:13–14). Section C begins at 5:15 with the confession of separation: "we have separated ourselves from the majority of the people" — the most explicit self-identification of the sectarian community's break from mainstream Judaism. The transition to scriptural exhortation (5:20–25) cites Deuteronomy's blessing-and-curse theology, urging the recipient to study Moses, the Prophets, and David. Hyphenated forms preserve Hebrew construct chains throughout.*
